parsed.explanation: Combined regime: protective division gives trans visitors robust state-sphere safety: anti-discrimination, facilities access, chosen names/pronouns, court-enforced care, consent-decree prison housing, refuge/safe-passage. But national entry, document markers, visa discrepancies, athlete ban, fraud lifetime-ineligibility threats, national facilities, and immigration/prison custody abuse remain operative and are not cancelled. For minors, national funding rules interrupt state youth-care coverage despite protective law. Adult alone: local reduced risk, border/federal elevated. Adult with minor: care/school friction and funding suspension add exposure. Absence of state violence data is uncertainty, not safety. Net: Elevated Risk, above hostile states due protective enforcement, below safer jurisdictions due national border/custody gate.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary passport/visa marker rules; new X markers barred; existing X valid until expiry. Visa discrepancy, athlete ban, fraud allegation for wilful sex misrepresentation; possible refusal, advisories, stranding, lifetime ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: No division immunity from national screening. Legal-aid FAQ and civil-liberties suit exist; some passport restrictions challenged.
entry_documents.interaction: Border screening precedes state protections; document mismatch can trigger refusal or investigation. Division safe-passage rules do not bind national entry officers.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse. National prisons adopt conversion-style rules, hormone removal. Fraud/entry dispute can escalate into custody.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Division consent decree improves state prison housing/health; courts remedy some custody harms. No documented protection from national or immigration custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: State custody protections do not shield visitors from federal/immigration detention; border discrepancy can become custody exposure.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; multiple other divisions have bans; four criminalise bathroom use via trespass; first arrest documented elsewhere.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division anti-discrimination/public-accommodation law, full facilities access, chosen-name/pronoun and uniform protections; top protective assessment.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State and private facilities safer; national or nationally funded sites can still impose binary restrictions; enforcement varies.

care_services.exposure: National funding freeze, youth-care pressure, insurance block, hospital subpoenas; public insurance suspends youth gender care from October 2026; providers face national pressure.
care_services.protection: Division protects gender-affirming care; highest court ordered hospital to resume blockers/hormones; safe-passage/refuge; expanded insurance coverage.
care_services.interaction: State courts can enforce adult/clinic care locally, but national funding conditions interrupt minor coverage and provider confidence.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism prioritises “radically pro-transgender” violent groups; orders target schools, teachers, “gender ideology”; removal of materials; official hostility.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Division hate-crime law covers gender identity/expression; gay-panic defence abolished; court remedies; protective equality enforcement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Local law enforcement likely protective; national rhetoric and funding pressure can elevate federal investigations and service disruptions.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor public insurance coverage suspended by national rule; national orders criminalise school social transition; district sports bans; unresolved ballot sports/surgery measures.
minors_guardians.protection: State anti-bullying, pronoun/uniform rules, court-ordered youth care, conversion-therapy ban, safe-passage protections; guardians not directly penalised by state law.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family travel can face denied or interrupted care, schooling friction, and national funding/criminalization pressure despite state protections.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-specific traveller violence rate or incident pattern documented; national bias data and hostile climate create uncertainty. Absence of evidence is not safety.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Division hate-crime statute, penalty enhancements, consent-decree remedies, public-accommodation enforcement; local complaints may receive support.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street harm uncertain and may be lower locally; federal agents, transport security, and outside jurisdictions remain less protective.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport/visa litigation unresolved; entry advisories shift; hospital compliance, document implementation, conversion-law status, ballot outcome, settlement terms unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid guidance, civil-liberties suit, state tribunals, court orders, top protective ranking, anti-discrimination remedies in the division.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Safety depends on which national rules are enforced at arrival and whether state courts/funding agencies continue compliance.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than the jurisdiction at 0.35–0.45? No, higher: 0.15-C involves morality sweeps, coerced statements, violence in custody and capital ambiguity. Here the division lacks criminal visitor-facing facility bans, protects care locally, and has court remedies; national entry/custody risk remains serious but execution is not documented credible.

Roughly similar: 0.55-B features extended border screening, discretionary refusal, delay, and slow remedies without credible custody. This jurisdiction has comparable national border uncertainty, worse fraud/custody exposure, but much stronger local facilities, care, anti-discrimination, and court enforcement, so the net is close to the 0.55 band.

Below 0.75-C: that anchor permits matching-marker passports, trained officers, brief detention release, and routine entry. Here national policy enforces binary markers, bars new X passports, uses discrepancy/fraud grounds, and has documented severe custody harms; state protections cannot offset the border and national-facility gate.

parsed.synthesis: The operative result is split: entry is nationally hostile, while local stay in the protective division is safer than the national average. Division laws on facilities, public accommodation, chosen names/pronouns, care, hate-crime response, and court-enforced remedies materially reduce risk once within that jurisdiction. However national passport/visa screening, entry refusals, fraud lifetime-ineligibility threats, national facility restrictions, immigration custody abuse, and youth-care funding blocks remain live. For a solo adult, local exposure is reduced but border/federal exposure is elevated; for a family, care interruption and schooling pressure add risk. Unknowns—court compliance, ballot measures, violence rates, and shifting guidance—do not create safety. Net: Elevated Risk, near but not above the midpoint of Reduced Risk.
